Billionaire Elon Musk has pledged to give every child in the United States two shares in his space exploration company, SpaceX, with one share coming from the company and the other from him personally. Musk announced the pledge in a post on X on Thursday, saying, “Every child in America will receive two SpaceX shares, one from the company and one from me personally.” The announcement followed a statement by SpaceX on Wednesday that it would donate one newly issued Class A share to every active Trump Account, a tax-advantaged investment account established for American children. SpaceX said Musk would personally match the number of shares donated by the company. However, it was not immediately clear whether his personal contribution would also be restricted to children with active Trump Accounts. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Add us to your Preferred Sources According to Reuters, SpaceX plans to transfer its shares in December, while Musk said his personal contribution would be made in June 2027, when his share lock-up period expires. The combined pledge is estimated to be worth nearly $18bn, based on SpaceX’s closing share price of $127.44 on Wednesday, according to Reuters. Trump Accounts are designed to help American children build long-term savings through investments. The White House said in October that nearly 70 million accounts had been opened. SpaceX President and Chief Operating Officer, Gwynne Shotwell, has also separately pledged more than two million of her shares to children under the initiative. Musk is the founder and chief executive of several technology companies, including electric vehicle maker Tesla, aerospace company SpaceX and artificial intelligence company xAI. He acquired Twitter in 2022 and later rebranded the social media platform as X. Through SpaceX, founded in 2002, Musk has pursued the development of reusable rockets and spacecraft, with the long-term ambition of making human life multi-planetary. The company has become a major contractor for NASA and plays a central role in the US commercial space industry. Musk, who is among the world’s richest people, has also made major political donations and publicly supported Donald Trump. He briefly served in the Trump administration as head of the Department of Government Efficiency before leaving the role in 2025.
